R1-01.verifier: R1-01 | Real | Important | Could not refute. Row 101 ("Make no further CO-A2 and no CO-A3; tell the customer it is not known whether the order was cancelled ... make CO-A4 with reason cancellation unknown") has no re-read, but the input requires one after every cancel timeout (packet R3 Q4: "re-read the order. Cancelled, continue to refund ... Shipped, report it ... Re-read fails, say outcome unknown"). If a lookup after the second CO-A2 shows the order cancelled, the row contradicts G-03 ("tells the customer an order was cancelled only when ... a lookup shows it cancelled"), CO-05 and CO-07 ("CO-A4 occurs in no other situation"). CO-S15 line 892 covers only an unanswered lookup. The missing order-absent branch of row 100 also stands, backed by cockburn-checklist.md line 74.
R1-01.status: fixed (in part); open for the still-open-after-two-cancels and order-absent branches

R1-02.verifier: R1-02 | Real | Important | Could not refute. Appendix A's outcome list ("the order is not cancelled: `OrderNotCancelled`"; "order not found: `OrderNotFound`") only permits these kinds of result. It does not make them true at that call. In CO-S17 row 3, the CO-A2 just before returned cancelled and set the status (Appendix A line 1524, Final state line 1023). In CO-S24, line 1411 says "Order <order> belongs to the customer", CO-A1 returned it, and Final state still asserts it exists. Neither injected outcome can be true of its scenario. Row 103 then tells the customer "the order is cancelled" right after the order system said it is not.
R1-02.status: fixed (CO-S17 row 3 and CO-S24 removed); open: the OrderNotFound and OrderNotCancelled failure-row clauses have no scenario consistent with the spec

R1-03.verifier: R1-03 | Not real | Important | Part (a): G-03 (line 24), "tells the customer a refund is pending or issued only when ... Otherwise it tells the customer the action was not done", requires "no refund was issued" in CO-S14 and CO-S15, where no CO-A3 was made. So following every rule, not only rows 100 and 101, gives that statement. Part (b): the same G-03 clause, plus packet R2 Q4 case 2 ("refund not issued, state known; agent reports it"), supports "the refund has not been issued" once the lookup in row 105 and CO-S20 shows the refund failed or absent.
R1-03.reason: Refutation read and accepted for part (a) only: G-03 makes "no refund was issued" a required statement. For part (b) the cited input, case 2, is the refund-error case, not the timeout-then-re-read case; for this case the input (Round 3 Q3) names the statement "say the refund is not confirmed yet", and G-03 is a spec line, not an input. The refutation answers part of the finding, so the finding stands for (b).
R1-03.status: fixed (part b); part (a) answered: G-03 requires it
